purpose: plan what will be tested, how, by whom and when, so test effort matches risk and the release decision has evidence
entry_criteria: Requirements and a release scope exist
Test environments and data are known or being planned
procedure: Define the test objectives from the release goals and the risks, and the exit criteria that will support the release decision.
Choose test levels and types per risk: unit, integration, system, performance, security and accessibility, and say what will be automated.
Trace requirements and risks to planned tests so gaps are visible.
Plan environments, data and tools, with their lead times and owners.
Estimate effort and schedule with the dependencies, and name who does what.
Agree how defects will be handled and reported, and review the plan with the product owner and developers.
deliverables: test plan with objectives and exit criteria
requirement and risk to test traceability
acceptance_criteria: Every high risk has planned tests
Environment and data lead times are planned
The plan was reviewed by product and engineering
validation_method: QA lead plan; product owner agreement on exit criteria.

validation.check: check each high-risk item in the risk list maps to at least one planned test
check each exit criterion has a number or a yes-no condition

failure_modes.mode: Plan lists activities but no criteria

failure_modes.response: Add tests or accept it formally

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A payments release plan lists exit criteria of zero open critical defects, all high-risk flows automated and passing, and a load test at 1.5 times peak; each is traced to a risk in the register.
